newsitem.title: USA: Volvo buys GM's interest in heavy truck venture.
newsitem.headline: Volvo buys GM's interest in heavy truck venture.

text.p: Swedish automaker AB Volvo said Wednesday it bought General Motors Corp.'s remaining interest in Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp. and will change the U.S. truckmaker's name to Volvo Trucks North America.
Financial details of the agreement between GM and AB Volvo were not disclosed.

Philip Romba, a spokesman at Volvo Trucks' headquarters in Greensboro, N.C., said Volvo has acquired 100 percent of the truckmaker's common stock. Most recently, GM had owned 13 percent of Volvo GM Heavy Truck, which builds heavy tractor-trailer type trucks.
GM will retain one seat on the unit's board of directors, Romba said. Volvo Trucks' Canadian affiliate also will eliminate GM from its name.
"We are now Volvo," Marc Gustafson, president and CEO of Volvo Trucks, said in a statement. "This investment is a concrete sign of Volvo's commitment to the North American truck market.
"Volvo Trucks is poised to build a stronger organisation which will enable it to achieve the same level of success as its parent has in other parts of the world," he added.
Romba said no major changes in Volvo Trucks' North American manufacturing, sales and administrative functions were anticipated as a result of the deal.

Volvo entered the U.S. heavy truck market in 1981 when it purchased assets of the bankrupt White Motor Co. In 1988, it combined those assets with GM's heavy truck business, creating Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp., which at the time was 76 percent owned by Volvo and 24 percent by GM.
The venture marketed trucks under the White-GMC name until 1995, when it switched to the Volvo name on all of its products.
